# HMAC-SHA-256 and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 where a key meets SHA-256's 64-byte
# block, which RFC 4231's and RFC 7914's vectors never reach: keys and
# passwords of 0, 63, 64 and 65 bytes -- one of 64 is the padded block as it
# is, one of 65 hashed first -- and PBKDF2 salts of 60 to 63 bytes, whose
# INT(1) ends the inner hash's second block or crosses into its third.
# Computed by Python's standard library, never by the code under test:
# every line below the comments is what this prints (Python 3.4 on).
#
#   python3 -I -c 'import hashlib, hmac
#   b = lambda n: bytes(range(n))
#   x = lambda v: v.hex() or "-"
#   m = b"what do ya want for nothing?"
#   for n in (0, 63, 64, 65): print("hmac", x(b(n)), x(m), hmac.new(b(n), m, "sha256").hexdigest())
#   for n in (0, 63, 64, 65): print("pbkdf2", x(b(n)), x(b"salt"), 2, hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", b(n), b"salt", 2, 32).hex())
#   for n in (60, 61, 62, 63): print("pbkdf2", x(b"password"), x(b(n)), 1, hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", b"password", b(n), 1, 32).hex())'
#
# One vector a line, its fields apart by a space, `-` for no bytes:
#   hmac <key> <message> <HMAC-SHA-256>
#   pbkdf2 <password> <salt> <c> <DK, its first 32 bytes>
